append.text: **Ps 45:8 = 45:12 (the refrain; also the Matins versicle *V. Dóminus virtútum nobíscum*) → *O Senhor dos poderes está conosco: * o nosso amparo é o Deus de Jacó*** — the row applied, still unruled; MS1932 and DRB have *dos exércitos* here (option 2); the blind reader heard 'the Lord who holds all power'. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 45:2 *Deus noster refúgium, et virtus* → *O nosso Deus é refúgio e poder*** — God's virtus → *poder*, kept apart from 45:4 *in fortitúdine ejus* → *força* two verses later; the familiar *refúgio e força* (MS1932, DRB) is the option. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 45:10 decided locally, as asked: *Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma* → *Quebrará o arco, e despedaçará as armas*** — the Greek has two verbs here (συντρίψει … συγκλάσει), so by D15's test the two stay two: contérere keeps *quebrar*, confríngere takes *despedaçar* (MS1932 *fará em pedaços*). Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 45:10 *confrínget arma* → *despedaçará as armas*** — the row's option used where contérere stands beside it (συγκλάσει, another Greek verb); see the row contérere.
**Ps 45:7 *dedit vocem suam, mota est terra* → *fez ouvir a sua voz, a terra se abalou*** — applied; the Latinist (v2 gate, minor) asked for *deu a sua voz*, refused (not said in Portuguese).
Ps 45:8 = 45:12 *suscéptor noster Deus Jacob* → *o nosso amparo é o Deus de Jacó* — applied; the blind reader listed *amparo* as unknown.

**Ps 45:5 *sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus* → *o Altíssimo santificou a sua tenda*** — the row applied. **For Gustavo:** the colon is sung alone of the Virgin (antiphon *Adjúvit eam Deus mane dilúculo; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus*, Immaculate Conception 12-08 and Our Lady Aparecida Brasilia/10-12; Dedication 12-10-Domus), where *tabernáculo* (option) carries the Marian sense. The blind reader heard *tenda* as a shop or stall as a second reading.
Ps 45:6 *mane dilúculo* → *de manhã, ao amanhecer* — both rows kept (this row and *dilúculo*'s); passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 45:2 *quæ invenérunt nos nimis* → *que nos encontraram sem medida* (= 37:9); the Latinist (v2 gate, minor) asked for *grandemente*, refused.

**Ps 45:9 *áuferens bella* → *ele tira as guerras*** — the participle made finite: the gerund *tirando* was heard by the blind reader as 'except for the wars'. The Latinist (v2 gate, minor) wanted the gerund back; held. *afastar* (stylist) refused as amovére's.
**Ps 45:6 *adjuvábit eam Deus* → *Deus há de auxiliá-la*** — draft 1 *Deus a auxiliará* lost the object in choir (*a au-*, the stylist); the periphrastic future keeps the enclitic audible.

terms: | vacáre (*Vacáte, et vidéte*) | parar (*Parai, e vede que eu sou Deus*) | open | Ps 45:11 only (grep). L&S 'be free from labour, at leisure'; σχολάσατε 'cease'. MS1932 *Parai*; safe under rule 3 (*parei*). The stylist asked *Aquietai-vos* (DRB 'be still', the Hebrew's 'let go') — kept as option; the blind reader heard 'stop'. |

| transférre | transportar (*e os montes forem transportados para o coração do mar*) | open | Ps 45:3. μετατίθεσθαι. *transferir* is an office's word, *trasladar* (MS1932) is for relics; the stylist's *levados* refused (addúcere's, D42). |
| sonáre | ressoar (*Ressoaram, e se perturbaram as águas deles*) | open | Ps 45:4 (ἤχησαν). MS1932 *Bramaram*, DRB 'roared' — the roar is the context's, not the word's; options. |

| ímpetus (flúminis) | ímpeto (*O ímpeto do rio alegra a cidade de Deus*) | open | Ps 45:5 (ὁρμήματα); sung alone as a versicle (C6-1, missa 02-05, Brasilia/08-30). The stylist's best line; the blind reader listed *ímpeto* as unknown and heard some violence in it. DRB 'stream', MS1932 *rio caudaloso*. |

| inclináre (of kingdoms) | inclinar-se (*e os reinos se inclinaram*) | open | Ps 45:7 (ἔκλιναν, 'gave way'). The blind reader heard 'bowed down in submission' first — the Latin's verb allows it. *se curvaram*, *vacilaram*, MS1932 *se humilharam* options. |

| *non commovébitur* with no subject named | *não se abalará* (pronominal, no gender) | open | Ps 45:6 *Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur*: the city or God; a participle (*abalada / abalado*) would choose. Sung alone in the Commons of Virgins and of the BVM. 20:8 (subject named) keeps *não será abalado*. |
